chapter_title: Chương 84: 0084【Có vẻ không đáng tin cậy】

segments.title: Chương 84: 0084【Có vẻ không đáng tin cậy】
segments.content:
"Hero Chen!"

"Bobo, long time no see."

"..."

Chen Guiliang ran into Xu Haibo at the school gate, and the two walked into the campus together.

On the way, they ran into a few more third-year students.

More than thirty people had already arrived in the classroom.

Of the rest, some had gone directly to repeat the year, while others already knew their scores.

You could check your results via text message yesterday, and even the cutoff scores for each admission tier had been released.

But Chen Guiliang didn't ask how to check, nor did he bother to, since he had to come to school to see his score and fill out his application anyway.

The form teacher, Liu Shuying, was all smiles. She waved and said, "Chen Guiliang, congratulations on your high score!"

He went over to Liu Shuying and received his gaokao score report, as well as a reference book for filling out his college application.

The score report wasn't sealed, printed on half a sheet of A4 paper.

When Chen Guiliang saw his total score, he was visibly stunned for a moment.

It was ridiculously high!

"What did you get?" Xie Yang quickly asked.

Chen Guiliang said, "628."

"Damn!"

"Freaking awesome."

"No way."

A series of gasps erupted in the classroom.

Li Yulin rushed over to look at the score report, and after confirming the score, he said, "Did you eat some kind of miracle... brain-booster?"

The class president, Li Rui, remained silent. He had performed very poorly on Chinese and the liberal arts comprehensive exam, and his total score was nearly 20 points lower than Chen Guiliang's.

"What about Wu Meng? What did Wu Meng get?" someone asked.

Wu Meng said with a smile, "639 (the provincial top scorer got 644)."

Three more students trickled in and went to get their score reports and reference books.

Seeing that almost everyone had arrived, Liu Shuying finally announced with a beaming face, "Wu Meng and a male student from Rongzhou High School are tied for first place in the city. Chen Guiliang is third in the city."

The guy who usually took turns with Wu Meng for first place in the city actually didn't score as high as Chen Guiliang this time.

Instead, it was a kid from the county town of Rongzhou who had an outstanding performance on the gaokao, quietly surging up to tie with Wu Meng for first place in the city.

Chen Guiliang's scores: Chinese 145, Math 113, English 110, Liberal Arts Comprehensive 260. Total score 628.

The provincial top scorer's scores: Chinese 145, Math 116, English 141, Liberal Arts Comprehensive 242. Total score 644.

His liberal arts comprehensive score pulled him up a ton this time, a full 18 points higher than the provincial top scorer!

Of course, his English was particularly weak, a result of pure guessing. With a total English vocabulary of just over a thousand words, what more could he expect?

The students' amazement didn't last long, and their attention soon turned to filling out their college applications.

Most of them had no idea what schools and majors they should apply for.

It was difficult to get information in those days, and the system of estimating scores and then applying based on actual scores kept changing, leaving students completely in the dark about the major universities.

Liu Shuying said, "You all need to read that college application reference book carefully. If you have any questions, come ask me, or call me if you can't find me. Now I'll briefly talk about some popular majors..."

While Liu Shuying was talking about university majors, Bian Guanyue sent a text message: "I was 9 points short of the Tier 1 cutoff."

"That's already amazing. Last year, you could only get into a Tier 3 school," Chen Guiliang replied.

"I was surprised too, but also a little disappointed. Just 9 points away from a Tier 1 university. If only I had worked a little harder."

"It's okay, you can choose a very good Tier 2 university."

"What's your score?"

"628."

"I asked around earlier. Peking University's admission score line is 620. You can get into Peking University even without special admission."

"That's almost impossible."

The gaokao in Chuanshu was just too competitive, and Tsinghua and Peking University offered very few spots.

Moreover, students from the Chuan region were excessively fond of applying to Peking University.

Take this year for example, 9 out of the top 10 liberal arts students in the province applied to Peking University, while Peking University was only recruiting a little over 20 liberal arts students in total from Chuanshu (including spots for independent recruitment).

Even though Chen Guiliang scored third in the city this time, exceeding Peking University's admission score line by 8 points, the possibility of getting into Peking University based on his score alone was almost zero.

If he didn't go through the New Concept Composition Contest route, with his score, it would actually be easier for Chen Guiliang to apply to Tsinghua—Tsinghua's admission score line was a full 8 points lower than Peking University's.

In other words, Chen Guiliang exceeded Tsinghua's admission score line by 16 points!

"Bobo, where are you applying?" Xie Yang asked.

Xu Haibo said, "Sichuan University, it's close to home. Plus, they have a lot of enrollment spots in Sichuan, so applying to Sichuan University is a safer bet."

Xu Haibo's gaokao score this time was more than 60 points above the Tier 1 cutoff, just right for Sichuan University. As long as he didn't choose an overly popular major, he would be accepted by Sichuan University one hundred percent.

Except for Chen Guiliang and Xu Haibo, all the other buddies from Room 302 bombed the exam.

Of the remaining six, four got into Tier 2 universities and two into Tier 3.

Xie Yang's score was even lower than Bian Guanyue's, placing him in the middle ranks of Tier 2.

Principal Yan had appeared in Class 11 at some point. The science stream results were a bit disappointing this year, but the liberal arts class had performed quite well.

Wu Meng was a sure bet for Tsinghua or Peking University, and Chen Guiliang could also get into Peking University through special admission.

Two students heading to Tsinghua or Peking University was something to be proud of.

"Student Wu Meng, congratulations, congratulations." Principal Yan extended his hand with a smile.

Wu Meng quickly stood up to shake it.

Principal Yan asked, "Are you planning to apply to Tsinghua or Peking University?"

"Peking University," Wu Meng said.

Principal Yan laughed, "Excellent, Chen Guiliang is also going to Peking University. You two can continue to be schoolmates."

He then walked towards Chen Guiliang, "Student Chen Guiliang, congratulations on your high score. To be honest, I'm very surprised. You actually managed to pass Peking University's admission score line through your own efforts alone. This shows that not only are you a good writer, but you also excel in all other subjects."

"I got lucky," Chen Guiliang said.

"Too modest," Principal Yan said. "When Peking University's admission notice arrives, you and Wu Meng will have to come to the county town. I've prepared a bus. You'll wear big red flowers, and we'll set off firecrackers all the way, circling the entire city twice."

Chen Guiliang: "..."

Principal Yan continued, "At that time, reporters from the TV station and newspaper will also be there, and the school will give you cash awards. After the school gives out its awards, you'll take a bus to the city. Boss Wu of the Pengfei Group is going to give every Tsinghua and Peking University student a twenty thousand yuan award!"

In a remote small city in 2004, the phenomenon of giving cash awards to Tsinghua and Peking University students was not common.

Everyone was very poor.

It was almost impossible to get rich through the gaokao, unlike later when rewards started at one hundred thousand yuan.

Principal Yan beckoned Wu Meng over and made pleasant small talk with them.

Bian Guanyue suddenly sent a text: "The admissions officer from Peking University just called me. I gave him your phone number."

Just as he finished reading the text, Chen Guiliang's phone rang.

Chen Guiliang said, "It's Peking University."

Principal Yan said happily, "Quick, answer it."

"Is this Student Chen Guiliang? I'm Zhu so-and-so, an admissions officer from Peking University."

"Hello, Teacher Zhu."

"How did you do on the exam this time?"

"628."

"That's very good, you've passed our admission score line in Chuanshu. Are you interested in coming to Peking University's Yuanpei Program?"

"When I applied for independent recruitment, I put down the Philosophy Department."

"You can change it even if you've already applied."

"Would Minister Cheng agree?"

"He said it depends on your personal preference. Our Yuanpei Program, you see, has a very special teaching method..."

Director Zhu suddenly raised his voice, "For the first three semesters, you don't choose a major, you're only divided into liberal arts and sciences. You can choose courses from any department in the entire Peking University, study whatever you want. Even for some required foundational courses, you can freely choose which class to attend."

Chen Guiliang said, "May I be so bold as to ask, is the Yuanpei Program an independent department?"

Director Zhu said, "It's not an independent department, but it doesn't belong to any department either. It's a very special existence at Peking University."

Chen Guiliang asked again, "So, you're saying the Yuanpei Program doesn't have its own department, teachers, classrooms, or dormitories?"

Director Zhu said, "All of Peking University's departments, classrooms, and teachers are yours to choose from. you can study liberal arts, science, and engineering courses at the same time."

"Can I understand it this way?"

Chen Guiliang's perspective on things was very unusual, "Those departments at Peking University are all properly-titled wives and concubines, and the students are the children of those wives and concubines. The Yuanpei Program, on the other hand, is just a serving girl, without even a place of her own. If I study in the Yuanpei Program, it's like being the child of a serving girl, and I'd still have to go mooch off the other wives and concubines for food and lodging?"

Director Zhu: "..."

The other end of the line fell into a brief silence.

Because Chen Guiliang had hit the nail on the head, directly seeing through the awkward position of the Yuanpei Program.

At this time, the Yuanpei Program had no department of its own, no teachers of its own, no classrooms of its own, no dormitories of its own... It had to piggyback on the resources of other departments for everything.

Were the other departments willing to be piggybacked on by the Yuanpei Program?

Some were supportive, some were opposed, and some were supportive on the surface but not very cooperative.

In a very few isolated classes, Yuanpei Program students were even ostracized by the teachers and students of their chosen courses!

There was a saying on the Peking University campus at this time: Don't marry a Guanghua girl, don't wed a Yuanpei man.

The girls from the Guanghua School of Management had sky-high standards; an ordinary Peking University man couldn't hope to measure up.

As for the men from the Yuanpei Program, they were all otherworldly geniuses, and also "prospects unknown" and very unreliable. Some didn't even know what major to specialize in by their junior year.

After organizing his words, Director Zhu continued, "Once you enter the Yuanpei Program, we will assign students a faculty advisor to help them select courses from across the entire university. There will also be part-time mentors assigned from time to time, all of whom are top scholars at Peking University. If you develop well, you can participate in your advisor's academic projects as early as the second semester of your sophomore year."

"Can I just randomly pick courses?" Chen Guiliang asked.

Director Zhu said, "Some students take liberal arts, science, engineering, and arts courses all at once. As long as you have the energy, you can choose whatever courses you want."

Chen Guiliang asked, "What about credits?"

Director Zhu said, "The credit requirements are a bit lower than for ordinary students. Also, the Yuanpei Program's academic system is very flexible. You can graduate normally in three years, and graduating in six years isn't considered a delay."

Chen Guiliang laughed, "So I can fool around in the Yuanpei Program for five years and then study in the last year?"

"As long as you've earned enough credits, no one will bother you." Director Zhu was just short of saying he could skip classes.

Director Zhu continued to coax him, "The living arrangements for the Yuanpei Program are also special. In one dorm room, there might be freshmen, sophomores, and juniors, and there might be liberal arts, science, and engineering students. You can have inter-year and interdisciplinary exchanges right in your own dorm room. If you're influenced by your roommates, you can also choose to transfer to any department in the sciences or engineering in your sophomore year. Of course, no matter which department you transfer to, you are still a Yuanpei Program student; your academic record is only formally transferred."

"That sounds rather unreliable," Chen Guiliang said.

Director Zhu said, "It all depends on your personal preference."

Chen Guiliang laughed, "But it's very interesting. I'm willing to give it a try."

"That's great," Director Zhu laughed heartily. "In your school, are there any other students with outstanding grades?"

Chen Guiliang said, "There's a city top scorer right in our class, and she plans to apply to Peking University."

Director Zhu said, "Then give him the phone."

Chen Guiliang handed the phone to Wu Meng, "The admissions officer from Peking University. He's trying to trick you into going."

He began to look forward to his university life. The Yuanpei Program was sure to have a lot of weirdos.

Chen Guiliang himself was a weirdo, able to meet his own kind
